name: Abu Ishaq al-Ilbiri
bio: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mas'ud al-Tujibi al-Ilbiri was an Andalusian jurist, ascetic and poet, named for Elvira (Ilbira); his family came from Hisn al-Uqab, and he made his name in Granada. He objected to the king's appointment of the Jewish vizier Ibn Naghrela, was exiled to Elvira, and wrote verse against the vizier, and the Sanhaja tribesmen rose against the vizier and killed him. His small diwan was printed from a manuscript in the Escorial; all his poetry is wisdom and admonition, and the best known is his Ta'iyya urging the pursuit of knowledge. He died around 460 AH (1068 CE).
